mappings.name: demo: transactionstatus EXPIRED, selected by AMOUNT rather than by order_id

comment: FILE: the outcomes examples/merchant-demo drives that transactionstatus.json
cannot reach from an end-to-end confirm. Added 2026-09-03 (Step 8, lane A) for
issue #11's 'drives the stub to succeeded and to failed/expired'.
THE PROBLEM THIS FILE SOLVES, and why it is not a scenario the way the MTN half
is. transactionstatus.json keys every case on `order_id`, which is
ChargeRef::reference_id -- a Uuid::new_v4() the confirm handler mints before it
commits the charge, and therefore not something a merchant can choose (the same
constraint mtn/mappings/demo-outcomes.json opens with). Orange's status call is a
POST, though, and its body is TransactionStatusRequest { order_id, amount,
pay_token } -- so `amount` travels on the status query itself, comes straight
from the merchant's own CreatePaymentIntent, and can be matched on directly. No
scenario, no state, no ordering constraint: this rail's outcomes are selected by
the request in front of WireMock, which is strictly better than the MTN half and
is only possible because of that one difference in the two protocols.
5001 XAF is a documentation amount in the same 500x block the settling outcome
uses (5000, which falls through to transactionstatus.json's priority-10 catch-all
SUCCESS). XAF is zero-decimal (docs/flows/money.md), so this is 5,001 FCFA.
IT IS AN AMOUNT AND SO IT IS GLOBAL: any charge on this rail for exactly 5001
XAF gets this answer, in a conformance run as much as in a demo. Nothing collides
today -- every conformance case and every integration test uses 5000
(adapter_conformance.rs, confirm_rails.rs, worker_e2e.rs, payment_intents.rs,
worker_recovery.rs, browser_checkout.rs) -- and a future test that wants a
settling Orange charge must not pick 5001 or 5002. Priority 4 keeps it BELOW the
reference-keyed cases (priority 1, lower number wins), so ...0404, ...05aa,
...0f01 and the rest still win whatever amount they carry.
EXPIRED -> payer_timeout (vpay_adapter_orange_money::mapping::STATUS_TABLE,
docs/flows/adapter-orange-money.md): the payer never entered the one-time code
before the hosted page aged out. This is the rail that actually documents
`EXPIRED`; MTN's equivalent outcome is COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION and its own
mapping file says why it is not spelled the same.
order_id is templated back out of the request so a captured body says which
charge was answered (--global-response-templating is on in compose.yml and in
vpay_testkit::containers::start_wiremock).
PRIORITY 4 IS NOW BETWEEN THREE THINGS, not two (2026-09-10, issue #58).
Below the reference-keyed cases in transactionstatus.json (1) and below
every mapping in stub-hosted-page.json that answers from a payer's
presence or action (3) -- a payer standing on the rail's page outranks an
amount a merchant chose, which is the whole of the fix. Above the two
unconditional rungs of the payer's window (6) and the catch-all (10), so
`just demo-walk` -- which opens no browser and never GETs the hosted page
-- still gets this answer on the FIRST rung and its timings did not move.

mappings.name: demo: transactionstatus FAILED, selected by AMOUNT rather than by order_id

response.body: {"status":"FAILED","order_id":"{{jsonPath request.body '$.order_id'}}","message":"Transaction refused by the payer's bank"}

comment: FAILED -> provider_error, carrying `message` through as the raw reason. NOT a
gap in the demo: Orange documents no sub-reason vocabulary for FAILED, so the
adapter refuses to guess and lands it in the 'unmapped, carries the raw reason'
bucket that docs/flows/failures.md says is a thing to ALERT on rather than a
settled mapping. The demo prints `provider_error` and says that out loud, because
a merchant integrating against this rail today will meet it.
The same body transactionstatus.json serves for reference ...0f02; this one is
reachable from a real confirm. 5002 XAF, same documentation block and same
global-by-amount caveat as the EXPIRED mapping above.

mappings.name: demo: the payer typed the EXPIRY test number on the rail's page

why: THE PAYER'S CHOICE, ON A RAIL THAT NEVER SEES A NUMBER. Added 2026-09-06
(exp22) so examples/shop can demonstrate a failed payment on Orange the way
it does on MTN -- by paying with a documented fake number.
MTN is a push rail: the MSISDN is in the merchant's own requesttopay body,
so mtn/mappings/demo-outcomes.json can key on it. Orange is a REDIRECT rail
and the number never reaches vpay at all -- the payer types it on Orange's
own page, after the charge has been submitted. So the steering has to happen
on the page, and it is carried to the status query by SCENARIO STATE.
THESE NOW WORK FROM A BROWSER (2026-09-10, issue #58). This comment said
the opposite, at length, and it was right when it was written: the stub
answered the first transactionstatus SUCCESS about 449 ms after the submit,
and a payer reached this form at about 12 s, so a run that typed
237600000400 came back PAID. What closed it is not here -- it is the payer's
window in stub-hosted-page.json, which answers PENDING from the submit and
then for a bounded chain of polls while a payer is on the page. This file
is unchanged in what it DOES; it simply now gets asked in time to matter.
The form that reaches these mappings is in stub-hosted-page.json, and so is
the `/pay` mapping that carries every OTHER number -- including the `#pay`
link, which sends no number at all. These two sit at priority 3 and that one
at 5, so a documented test number wins.
Proven against a real container, driving this page and this form, by
`a_test_number_typed_on_the_rails_hosted_page_reaches_the_documented_outcome`
in backends/tests/conformance -- which since 2026-09-10 also asserts the
PENDING answers that come first, so a chain shortened to zero fails it. The
browser half is the Orange legs of frontends/tests/e2e's shop specs.
STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL, like MTN's. One scenario per container means two Orange
charges in flight against one stub share it, and the wrong one could be
failed. The demo drives one payment at a time.

mappings.name: demo: the armed expiry answers EXPIRED once, then disarms

why: Answered ONCE and then disarmed (newScenarioState `Started`), for the reason
MTN's file gives: EXPIRED and FAILED are terminal, so the worker settles on
this answer and asks nothing more about this charge, and leaving the scenario
armed would make the NEXT charge in the walk inherit an outcome nobody chose.
PRIORITY 3 is deliberate and sits between two things: BELOW the order_id-keyed
mappings in transactionstatus.json (priority 1), which the conformance suite
depends on and which must keep winning; and ABOVE both the amount-keyed demo
mappings in this file (priority 4) and the catch-all SUCCESS (priority 10).
A container whose payer has never used this form cannot reach these mappings
at all -- no state, no answer.
-> payer_timeout (vpay_adapter_orange_money::mapping::STATUS_TABLE,
docs/flows/adapter-orange-money.md). The same body the amount-keyed
mapping above serves for 5001; this one is reachable from a payer.

mappings.name: demo: the armed refusal answers FAILED once, then disarms

response.body: {"status":"FAILED","order_id":"{{jsonPath request.body '$.order_id'}}","message":"Transaction refused by the payer's bank"}

why: Answered ONCE and then disarmed (newScenarioState `Started`), for the reason
MTN's file gives: EXPIRED and FAILED are terminal, so the worker settles on
this answer and asks nothing more about this charge, and leaving the scenario
armed would make the NEXT charge in the walk inherit an outcome nobody chose.
PRIORITY 3 is deliberate and sits between two things: BELOW the order_id-keyed
mappings in transactionstatus.json (priority 1), which the conformance suite
depends on and which must keep winning; and ABOVE both the amount-keyed demo
mappings in this file (priority 4) and the catch-all SUCCESS (priority 10).
A container whose payer has never used this form cannot reach these mappings
at all -- no state, no answer.
-> provider_error, and that is the honest mapping rather than a gap:
Orange documents NO sub-reason vocabulary for FAILED, so the adapter's
STATUS_TABLE maps it to ProviderError with the raw message alongside.
A stub answering `NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS` here would be this repository
inventing a rail vocabulary; examples/shop/README.md says so where it
lists what this rail cannot express.
